html:
Trinidad Carnival is the festival held on the Monday and Tuesday before Lent. French planters brought masked balls after the Cedula of Population, and after emancipation in 1838 the freed people made the street festival their own.

They brought canboulay, a night procession with torches recalling cane fires. Attempts by British police to ban it led to the Canboulay riots of 1881. Carnival then grew around calypso songs, steel bands and costumed masquerade bands.

Trinidad's migrants took the festival abroad. The Notting Hill Carnival in London, begun in the 1960s, and carnivals in Toronto, New York and Miami follow its form. It is the centre of the island's year and its music business.
